changes.after: The derive instruction can ask Rust to write a comparison for a struct.

before: #[derive(...)] requests generated implementations when every field supports the necessary behavior. Debug supports {:?} formatting; PartialEq supports ==. Deriving does not bypass a field’s trait requirements.

Clone explicitly duplicates a value according to its implementation. Copy permits implicit bitwise value copying and requires Clone; it cannot be derived for a struct containing String. An all-u32 record can derive both, but owning String data needs ownership-aware treatment.
Expected output or behavior: true. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Try deriving Copy for a separate String-owning struct and inspect the rejection. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
